title: Start or catch up a project from a golden path, through an interview sized to its scale
intent: Every project in ApexYard starts from, or catches up to, the same quality floor. The /scaffold skill serves new projects and /handover. It interviews the owner one question at a time. The depth of the interview follows the project's scale. Every question offers a recommended answer with a plain reason, so a non-engineer can accept safe defaults. The skill records the answers in a scaffold spec and recommends a stack. A tested golden path is preferred, and any other stack gets the same floor. It generates a hardened local project whose CI enforces the quality gates, a dependency audit and the fitness functions that the spec sets. For an existing repository, it sizes each gap by scale and proposes the fixes through a PR. It writes a draft infrastructure recommendation and a monthly cost estimate, and it never applies them. It never pushes, never creates a remote repository without the owner's yes, and never writes a secret. Review findings on generated projects feed back into the starter and the interview.

outcomes.title: The /scaffold interview matches its depth to the project's scale, and every question offers a recommended answer.
outcomes.intent: A non-engineer can accept safe defaults, and an engineer answers only what is open.

outcomes.title: /scaffold recommends a stack from the answers. Every project gets the stack-agnostic floor, and a golden-path stack also gets its tested starter.
outcomes.intent: A few tested golden paths are the paved roads, not the only roads. Any stack starts at the same quality floor.

outcomes.title: /handover uses the same interview to fill the gaps of an existing repository, sized by scale, through a PR.
outcomes.intent: Existing repositories catch up to the golden path.

outcomes.title: /scaffold writes a draft infrastructure recommendation and a monthly cost estimate matched to scale and budget, and never applies the infrastructure.
outcomes.intent: Every stack gets best-practice infrastructure advice and a cost estimate, also when no starter template exists for it.

outcomes.title: /scaffold generates python-fastapi and go-data-pipeline projects, names each gap that no bundle covers, and shares its copy script with /handover.
Generated CI checks layer boundaries and the bundle-size budget, and one file lists each gate and the spec answer that set it.

outcomes.intent: Each project the framework scaffolds makes the next one safer.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The first question asks for the scale: demo or prototype, small product, or production service. A demo asks at most 5 questions. A production service asks every question.
The interview asks one question at a time through AskUserQuestion. Each question shows the recommended answer first, with one plain-language sentence that gives the reason.
The answer 'Not sure, recommend for me' records the recommended value, its reason and the mark recommended. The skill never records a silent guess.
Before it asks, the skill reads the tech_stack block of onboarding.yaml and any PRD for the project. It asks only what those files leave open.
The skill writes the answers to a scaffold spec file that a JSON schema validates. The spec records the scale and the source of each answer: owner, recommendation, onboarding or PRD.

The interview asks for service shape, language, deployment target, coverage floor and design direction. It recommends a stack from the shape, team skills, scale and deployment target, with a plain reason. The answer none yet for design or deployment adds an open question to the project plan notes.
A rule table in the framework maps the spec to a golden path. In o2 the table holds typescript-nextjs with a starter. A spec that no golden path fits gets the custom start of ac2-16, not a stop.
The skill shows the pick and the spec answers that decided it. The owner confirms or overrides the pick, and the skill records the choice in the spec.

The typescript-nextjs bundle ships a starter directory with a minimal source tree, its tool configuration and exact pinned versions. The bundle VERSION gets a minor bump. Every dependency, development tools included, has an exact version. The skill audits each version that a generator proposes before it pins the version.
One copy script copies the starter, handbooks, CI files and topology anchor into workspace/<name>/. The generated tree passes check-secrets.sh.
Generated CI fails below the coverage floor and on a lint, typecheck or build fault. The floor is 80 percent, or the spec value when it is higher.
Generated CI runs a dependency audit. A high or critical advisory in a production dependency fails the build.
Before the skill picks a tool that needs install scripts or network access at install time, it checks the build environment. When the check fails, it picks a fallback and records both in the AgDR.
For a web service shape, the starter sets session cookies HttpOnly and SameSite with one rule for Secure. State-changing API routes accept JSON only. Errors use problem+json with stable codes.
One command migrates, seeds and starts the project locally. One command resets local data to the seed.
A typescript-nextjs fixture has one seeded fault for each gate. A framework CI test proves each gate fails on its fault and passes on the clean starter. The PR records the added CI time.
The /handover harnessability assessment rates the generated typescript-nextjs project high on all five dimensions.
The skill writes one proposed AgDR for the scaffold. The AgDR lists each stack choice and the spec answers that drove it.
/scaffold is a bootstrap skill, and its bootstrap scope names each path it writes. Hakim reviews that scope and approves it before the slice PR merges.

The skill text and each generated Markdown file pass bin/check-writing-profile.sh with zero faults. CLAUDE.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/whats-inside.md and topologies/README.md list /scaffold with correct skill counts.
For an existing repository, /handover offers /scaffold gap-fill mode. It starts only after the owner says yes. A no leaves no files.
The gap-fill report compares the repository with the closest topology. It lists missing CI pipelines, quality gates and fitness functions, with reasons for the topology choice.
After the owner says yes, gap-fill mode proposes the missing additions on a branch and opens a PR for review.
Gap-fill mode never overwrites an existing file without an explicit yes from the owner for that file.
The gap-fill report records harnessability scores before and after the proposed changes. It uses the same five dimensions and shows the change in each score.
Each gap in the report has a size from the scale: must, should or later. The interview asks only about gaps and recommends an answer for each gap.
The interview asks for expected scale, monthly budget and compliance needs. Each question accepts unknown, and the skill never guesses a value.
For every host, the skill writes a draft infrastructure recommendation, also when no IaC template exists. It names each service, its size and the reason from the spec answers.
For an AWS host, the draft includes Terraform that passes terraform validate and tflint without cloud credentials. A check also fails on any non-ASCII string in the .tf files.
The generated Terraform CI has its apply job off. Only the owner turns it on, in a later PR.
The cost estimate gives low, expected and high monthly figures, the three largest cost drivers and the assumptions. When the expected figure exceeds the budget, it names the drivers to cut.
The estimate uses a static price table with a price date and states that the figures are not a quote. Framework CI fails when the price date is older than 6 months.
The skill never runs terraform apply or any cloud write call, and it needs no cloud credentials.
The rule table adds python-fastapi and go-data-pipeline. When the language answer is unknown, the skill asks about team skills and recommends a language from them.
The skill lists each spec need that no bundle covers as a gap, for example a second service shape. When no bundle fits, it offers a custom start and an upstream topology request.
The python-fastapi and go-data-pipeline bundles ship starter directories with exact pinned versions. Each bundle VERSION gets a minor bump.
Generated CI for each new bundle enforces the ac2-6 gates. Each bundle fixture installs only its own toolchain, and the PR records the added CI time.
/handover step 5.5 calls the ac2-5 copy script. A regression test proves /handover writes the same files for an existing repository as before.
A framework script computes the five harnessability scores. typescript-nextjs scores high on each dimension. The other bundles reach their best reachable bucket on each dimension.
Generated CI checks architecture layer boundaries for each topology bundle. TypeScript projects use the dependency-cruiser config from the harness golden-path initiative.
For a web shape, the interview asks for a bundle-size budget. When the spec names one, generated CI fails above it.
The generated project has one fitness-functions file that lists each gate, its threshold and the spec answer that set it.
Each new gate has a seeded fault in each bundle fixture. The framework CI test proves the gate fails on its fault and passes on the clean case.
For a new fork, /onboard offers /scaffold when the owner selects start a new project. It recommends /scaffold and keeps light registration.
The skill adds a registry entry that passes validation. After the owner says yes, it creates the remote with a README-only default branch and opens the scaffold as a PR.
At the end, /scaffold offers /walking-skeleton and passes the layers and the deploy target from the spec as defaults.
After /write-spec produces an approved PRD for a new product, it offers /scaffold. The interview reuses PRD answers and asks only for gaps.
The /write-spec offer starts /scaffold only after the owner says yes. A no leaves no files.
The /onboard interview reuses recorded answers and asks only for gaps. The offer starts /scaffold only after the owner says yes. A no leaves no files.
When an ORBIT slice handoff needs a new repository, it offers /scaffold. The spec uses the initiative outcomes and constraints without asking recorded answers again.
The ORBIT handoff offer starts /scaffold only after the owner says yes. A no leaves no files.
A finding that traces to the starter or the interview becomes a scaffold change: a starter fix, a new question or a new check.
Each scaffold change of this kind adds one changelog line. The line names the class of finding and never names the project.

For a stack with no golden path, the custom start applies the stack-agnostic floor with the stack's own tools. The floor covers CI gates, a dependency audit, exact pins, the security baseline and the general handbooks. The skill marks the project custom and drafts a golden-path request for the owner to file.
